_comment: Tier-2 for fourc fluid#: 4C's time-integration enums are SECTION-DEPENDENT. FLUID DYNAMIC/TIMEINTEGR has 'Af_Gen_Alpha, Np_Gen_Alpha, BDF2, One_Step_Theta, Stationary' (underscored, Af_/Np_ prefixes). SCALAR TRANSPORT DYNAMIC/TIMEINTEGR has 'Gen_Alpha, BDF2, One_Step_Theta, Stationary' (underscored, no prefix). STRUCTURAL DYNAMIC/DYNAMICTYPE has 'GenAlpha, OneStepTheta, Statics, ...' (CamelCase). THERMAL DYNAMIC/DYNAMICTYPE has 'GenAlpha, OneStepTheta, Statics, Undefined' (CamelCase). The earlier catalog used bare 'GenAlpha' / 'OneStepTheta' uniformly for fluid + scatra — wrong, fails at YAML parse with 'Could not match this input'. Verified empirically 2026-06-01. MUTATION CONTROL (T2_MUTATE=1, re-runnable): BARE_CAMELCASE and UNDERSCORED are swapped. bare_camelcase_in_fluid=[], bare_camelcase_in_scatra=[], underscored_in_struct=[] and underscored_in_thermal=[] all disappear, replaced by the non-empty intersections that state the same section-boundness from the other side. Proved KILLED 2026-08-07. Also repaired on 2026-08-07: the fixture read only 4C_schema.json, a post-build product of create-schema-files that this host's build never generated, so it reported 'FAIL: 4C_schema.json not found' and was red for an environmental reason; it now falls back to 4C_metadata.yaml, the generator's own input, which the build tree does carry.

_mutation.note: remove the assumption that the probe measures at all: SWAP the two probe sets, so the fixture asks whether the underscored names are in fluid/scatra (they are) and whether the CamelCase names are in structural/thermal (they are). All four '...=[]' expectations then report non-empty sets and the fixture must go red. The mutant's output is the positive half of the same claim, which is the only way to control an inventory fixture whose subject is 4C's own enums.
